doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: Hampton's big band, small groups and showmanship
summary: Mullins played in the big band and in small combos with Hampton, who was an amazing performer on vibes, piano and drums.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Was this — I can almost picture it. Was this the big band or was it a smaller group?

The big band, yeah. Because he had a big band and sometimes he didn’t use the big band if he would go or something, he would just call me and the bass player. Or sometimes it would just be me — it would just be me and him playing. Or sometimes he’d call me and a bass player and a sax player. You know?
He was a real showman, wasn’t he? On stage?
Tell me about some of the stuff he would do.

He was amazing man. People would be out there looking mean. “Come on, start the music” you know what I mean and all that. And he would just get out there and he’d start playing them vibes and then by the time he’d get through they’d be standing up doing this [stomps] on the floor with their feet. He was amazing. An amazing performer.
Did he come over to the piano on occasion and do his two finger thing?
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. And do it very well, man, just like he was playing the vibes.
And he was a drummer too.
A drummer, yeah. Well his legs were kind of going on him. But up on top, whew. His two hands on top, man, was furious.
